title: PWM Tone Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: PWM
Sound
Frequency
Duty Cycle
Musical Notes
description: Interactive p5.js MicroSim where frequency and duty-cycle sliders shape a PWM square wave on an oscilloscope, a piano keyboard highlights the nearest note, and a Play button sounds the tone with the Web Audio API.

educational.topic: PWM sound: frequency, pitch and duty cycle
learningObjectives: Explain that frequency sets pitch and duty cycle sets how long each cycle is on
Calculate the period, on time and off time for a given frequency and duty cycle
Apply f = 440 x 2^(n/12) to find the frequency of a note

keyQuestions: What happens to the frequency when a note goes up one octave?
Does changing the duty cycle change the pitch?
Why is there no sound at 0% or 100% duty?
commonMisconceptions: A higher duty cycle makes a higher pitch (pitch depends only on frequency)
Notes are evenly spaced in hertz (each semitone multiplies the frequency by about 1.0595)
assessmentOpportunities: Calculate the period and on time for a given frequency and duty
Predict a note's frequency with the formula and verify it

controls.label: Play / Stop
controls.description: Starts or stops the tone. The MicroSim opens silent; sound starts only after this click.
